concept.name: Option series
concept.definition: An option series is the set of option contracts of the same type (all calls or all puts) on the same underlying instrument that share the same expiration date and the same strike (exercise) price — i.e., a single line of an option chain, such as 'XYZ January 100 calls'.
concept.intuition: If the option chain is the menu, a series is one specific dish: one underlying, one expiry, one strike, one side (call or put).
concept.mechanics: All contracts within a series are fungible: any long contract in the series can be offset by selling any contract in the same series. Exchanges list new series as the underlying price moves and as new expiration cycles approach; open interest and volume are reported per series.
concept.failure_modes: Off-the-run series (far dated, deep ITM/OTM) can have zero open interest and no active market maker quotes, making them practically untradable at fair prices.
concept.misconceptions: A 'series' is not a spread or a sequence of trades — it is simply the identifier for all contracts sharing underlying, type, strike, and expiration.
concept.example: The 'AAPL Dec 2026 200 call' series groups every AAPL December 2026 call contract struck at $200; buying and later selling that same series closes the position.

citations.source: CFTC Glossary — A Guide to the Language of the Futures Industry
